title: Boundary cohomology of an open-extended pro-etale injective on a proper scheme
statement:
Let $Q=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] in the universes of its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Assume that $R$ is w-contractible in the following explicit sense: every faithfully flat weakly etale ring map $R\to R'$ admits an $R$-algebra retraction $R'\to R$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Let $z:Z\hookrightarrow Q$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with complementary quasi-compact open immersion $e:E\hookrightarrow Q$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume every point of $Q$ specializes to a point of $Z$, meaning that for every $x\in Q$ the closure of $\{x\}$ meets $Z$.
Let $p:P\to Q$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], set $P_E=P\times_Q E$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $h:U\hookrightarrow P_E$ be an open immersion whose image is also closed. Assume the composite $j:U\hookrightarrow P_E\hookrightarrow P$ is a quasi-compact open immersion. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $J$ be an injective sheaf of modules over the constant sheaf $A_U$ on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Assume in addition that $J$ has etale origin: there are a sheaf $J_0$ of $A$-modules on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] and an isomorphism $\nu_U^*J_0\cong J$, where $\nu_U$ is the site-comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Then its extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero] satisfies
$$H^q(P_{\mathrm{proet}},j_!J)=0\qquad(q>0).$$
Here cohomology means the right derived functors of global sections in the category of constant-$A$ module sheaves, computed by an injective resolution [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-sp-injective-resolutions].

source.place: Clause (b), compactification independence: agent-extracted boundary-cohomology sublemma of the pro-etale injective-acyclicity obligation. Etale motivation only: literature/stacks-project/more-etale.tex, Tag 0F7B, label lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, case (b), the boundary-fibre vanishing. Pro-etale Tag 09AG, label lemma-jshriek-zero, gives only degree-zero specialization vanishing, not this higher-cohomology assertion. Neither tag is claimed to prove this pro-etale statement.

proof.text:
Put $F=j_!J$ and choose the supplied witness $\alpha:
u_U^*J_0\cong J$. By [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] there is an isomorphism $
u_P^*(j^{\mathrm{et}}_!J_0)\cong j_!
u_U^*J_0\cong F$. Regard both sheaves as complexes concentrated in degree zero: their degree-zero cohomology is the sheaf and all other cohomology is zero. This is an etale-origin witness for $F[0]$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Exactness of $j_!$ identifies its action on these degree-zero complexes with the sheaf $F$. No injectivity of $J_0$ is required.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison; bounded-below witness concentrated in degree zero.

proof.text: Let $a:P_Z=P\times_Q Z\hookrightarrow P$ and $b:P_E\hookrightarrow P$ be the base changes of $z$ and $e$. They are complementary closed and open immersions, and $b$ is quasi-compact. These statements follow respectively from [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change]; complementarity is the inverse-image equality of the two subsets. Since $j=bh$, the adjunction of [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction] identifies $j_!$ with $b_!h_!$: both are left adjoint to $h^*b^*=j^*$, and the adjunction bijections give the canonical identification. Thus $a^*F=a^*b_!h_!J=0$ by the $i^{-1}j_!=0$ clause of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] on $P$. All coefficient rings are the inverse images of the same constant ring $A$.

source.place: Tags 09AH and 09BN, complementary immersion functors; base-change stability of immersions and quasi-compactness.

proof.text: Write $p_Z:P_Z\to Z$ for the projection. Apply [thm-weil-pbc-finite-level-proetale] to the Cartesian square with horizontal arrows $a,z$, vertical arrows $p_Z,p$, and input $F[0]$. Properness of $p$ and finiteness of the discrete commutative ring $A$ are hypotheses of the item; step 1 supplies exactly the etale-origin witness required by the theorem. It gives $z^*Rp_*F[0]\cong Rp_{Z,*}a^*F[0]=0$ by step 2. The derived direct image carries zero to zero because its additive injective-resolution construction carries the zero resolution to zero.

source.place: Tag 09C9, theorem-proper-base-change, with coefficient ring A and ideal 0; no constructibility assumption.

proof.text: For an integer $q$ set $G_q=\mathcal H^q(Rp_*F[0])$. The module inverse image $z^*$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation]. Applying it to the kernels and images defining cohomology therefore gives $z^*G_q=\mathcal H^q(z^*Rp_*F[0])=0$. Apply the exact open-closed sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] on $Q$ to $G_q$. Its final term is zero, so its counit identifies $G_q\cong e_!e^*G_q$. The hypothesis that $e$ is quasi-compact is exactly the hypothesis needed for this sequence.

source.place: Tags 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open, and 09BL, closed inverse-image evaluation and exactness.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-shriek-specialization-zero] with $X=Q$, $U=E$, the given closed immersion $z$, and the affine site object $V=Q$ with its identity map. An open immersion is weakly etale, $E\times_Q Z$ is empty, and every point of $Q$ specializes into $Z$ by hypothesis. It gives $(e_!H)(Q)=0$ for every abelian sheaf $H$ on $E$. The same vanishing holds for constant-$A$ module sheaves: [def-weil-extension-by-zero] defines their extension by sheafifying the identical zero-or-one-summand presheaf, and [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] explicitly takes the underlying abelian sheafification and then extends the scalar action. Forgetting the action therefore gives exactly the abelian extension used by the lemma. With $H$ underlying $e^*G_q$, step 4 yields $G_q(Q)=0$.

source.place: Tag 09AG, lemma-jshriek-zero; sites-modules.tex module-sheafification construction. This is degree-zero vanishing of G_q, not a direct higher-cohomology use of 09AG.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-wcontractible-affine-weakly-contractible] with $X=Q$ and its identity site object. The ring-retraction assumption in the item makes this object weakly contractible in the full small pro-etale site, with the stipulated universes. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-weakly-contractible-evaluation-exact], evaluation at this object on constant-$A$ module sheaves preserves homology. In particular, for every complex $C^\bullet$ of such sheaves, $\mathcal H^q(C^\bullet)(Q)=H^q(C^\bullet(Q))$.

The small-site module category on $P$ is Grothendieck by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], hence has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Choose an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ with $I^n=0$ for $n<0$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; by definition $H^q(P_{\mathrm{proet}},F)=H^q(I^\bullet(P))$. By part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] the bounded-below injective complex $I^\bullet$ is K-injective. In [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], $Rp_*(QI^\bullet)=Q(p_*I(I^\bullet))$ for the functorial K-injective resolution $I^\bullet\to I(I^\bullet)$. This is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injective complexes, hence a homotopy equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; the additive termwise functor $p_*$ preserves homotopy equivalences, so $p_*I^\bullet$ represents $Rp_*F[0]$, as $QI^\bullet\cong F[0]$. The direct-image section formula of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] gives $(p_*I^n)(Q)=I^n(P)$, since $P\times_Q Q=P$. Thus, by step 6 and then step 5, $H^q(P_{\mathrm{proet}},F)=H^q(I^\bullet(P))=H^q((p_*I^\bullet)(Q))=G_q(Q)=0$. This proves the requested $q>0$ vanishing (and also degree zero). This argument resolves $F$ on $P$ and never assumes that $j_!J$ is injective.

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the arbitrary-pro-etale-injective statement is false. report.md gives a regular nodal elliptic degeneration, the profinite-cyclic-cover / infinite-cyclic-cover coset sheaf, and an injective-envelope argument giving nonzero H^1(j_!J). Restore the etale-origin hypothesis of the source coefficient class. Split the corrected claim into open comparison, disjoint restriction, finite-level proper base change, base support, specialization-zero and exact evaluation. No new nodes. Parent arbitrary-injective callers are not discharged by this correction.
split_report.blueprint: Repairs the boundary obligation extracted below cor-exc-base-change-open-immersion-general. The current blueprint works on the etale-origin/localizing coefficient class; its old clause (b) does not assert arbitrary-sheaf pro-etale proper base change. The corrected proof uses the existing proper-base-change chapter as a generic comparison tool, without the circular arbitrary-open acyclicity nodes.

tool_uses.why: Step 1 uses compatibility of comparison inverse image with open extension by zero. The existence unit does not prove this sheaf-comparison identity.
Step 1 packages a degree-zero etale complex and the comparison isomorphism into exactly the input datum of finite-level proper base change.
Step 1 uses exactness to identify the termwise extension of the degree-zero complex with the derived extension; this is the general open-operation exactness tool.
Step 2 uses stability of closed immersions under arbitrary base change, a generic geometric fact outside the existence unit.
Step 2 uses stability of open immersions under arbitrary base change, a generic geometric fact outside the existence unit.
Step 2 uses quasi-compactness of the base change of E to check the open-closed localization hypothesis; the existence unit supplies no different quasi-compactness theorem.
Step 2 uses the open adjunction twice to identify the composite extension by zero, without assuming any higher-cohomology result.
Steps 2 and 4 use only disjoint restriction and the module sheaf short exact localization sequence, not derived proper base change or arbitrary-injective acyclicity.

Step 3 uses finite-ring proper base change exclusively for the etale-origin witness built in step 1. The original arbitrary-injective route is false, as the report counterexample shows; this comparison theorem supplies the corrected coefficient-class argument, not a replacement of the existence unit.
Steps 3 and 7 use the ordinary uncompleted pushforward and its section formula to compute cohomology of the actual sheaf, with no completion or coefficient-category change.
Step 4 uses exact module inverse image for the closed immersion, to commute it with cohomology; no conservativity of geometric stalks is assumed.
Step 5 uses the affine degree-zero specialization vanishing only after showing each cohomology sheaf is an open extension; this avoids misusing it as higher vanishing.
Step 5 identifies the defining module extension presheaf with the underlying abelian extension presheaf for an open immersion.
Step 5 uses the explicit underlying abelian sheafification construction to transfer specialization vanishing from abelian to module sheaves.
Step 6 converts the item's ring-retraction assumption into surjectivity of evaluation on all sheaf epimorphisms, not only etale sheaves.
Step 6 uses preservation of homology by module evaluation at the weakly contractible affine object.
Step 7 uses the Grothendieck property of small-site module sheaves. The fixed site universes make the underlying category small in the sheaf universe.
Step 7 obtains enough injectives in that module category from its Grothendieck property; this is a generic homological algebra tool.
Step 7 uses its degree bound n=0 and its bounded-below K-injectivity clause for an honest injective resolution.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NA-139067506 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full, the base statement, the citer lem-sp-proetale-open-injective-proper-acyclic, all 20 cited statements, Stacks 09AG/09C9/0982 and HHL Cor. 4.19 and Rem. 7.15. The base statement ('J need not have etale origin') is false. I checked the delivered counterexample step by step. Setup: Q=Spec k[[t]] is w-contractible by 0982; P is the regular cubic degeneration with a nodal fibre C; the ℤ-chain cover of C lifts by 0A48 to an integral pro-étale Ẑ-torsor T̃. Take F=F_p[T̃/ℤ]. Γ(P,F)=0, because π0^cond(T̃)=* and Ẑ-invariants of F_p[Ẑ/ℤ] vanish. Restricted to C, F has a nonzero section. Γ(P,G)→Γ(C,i^*G) is injective by 09AG on the cover by localizations at units mod t. With J=j^*I for an injective envelope I of F, this gives H^1(P,j_!J)≠0. The added etale-origin hypothesis is a visible E7 correction of a non-target agent-extracted node, and the corrected statement is true. Steps 1–6 check against their cited statements: 09AF comparison gives the witness; open-closed gives a^*j_!=0; finite-level pro-étale PBC (09C9 with I=0) gives z^*Rp_*F=0; the cohomology sheaves are e_!-extended; 09AG gives G_q(Q)=0; evaluation at the w-contractible Q is exact. I accept the tool_uses. FIX (C4): step 7 cited lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective for 'p_*I^• represents Rp_*F'. That node concerns an abstract D^+ Kan extension, not the operations Rp_*. I rewrote step 7 to use an injective resolution, K-injectivity (dplus-representative (2)) and lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived, and updated uses, proof_deps and tool_uses (whole file in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-smooth-purity/). Maintainer note: the citer lem-sp-proetale-open-injective-proper-acyclic is false by the same example, since evaluating R^1p_* at Q gives H^1≠0. Its step citing this item no longer matches, and its chain (lem-sp-proper-open-derived-support, lem-sp-fullcd-ambient-adjoint) needs a HUMAN.md entry.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
